main_body: A wooden pew drawn as a wide, horizontal bench. It is mostly a flat front view of horizontal plank bands (dark and light brown stripes) between two vertical side posts. Nothing reads as a seat surface seen from above.
top_band: Row 0-1 is a dark brown strip, followed by mid-brown planks. The lighter tan/orange bands at rows 6-8 and 10-11 look like backrest slats or the seat edge, not a foreshortened top surface. No clear lighter top band sits above a distinct front face.
evidence: Reading one column through the middle: dark brown at rows 0-1, mid brown at rows 2-5, dark at rows 6-7, orange-tan at rows 8-9 (1-2 row bands), brown, orange-tan again at rows 10-11, then dark and brown to row 14. These are stacked horizontal planks seen straight on, with side posts at both ends. No horizontal seat surface is visible from above, and there are no legs or set-back front under a top. This matches the front-elevation failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has a few brown tones (dark brown, mid brown, orange-tan) and some faint grain flecks on the light bands. Large stretches of mid-brown plank are flat fills. Compared with the stall and well references, which carry 5-6 shading steps and rich per-tile texture, it is much thinner. The outlines are dark brown rather than black, which fits the standard, but the overall tile density is low.
